passages: At Elm School, students used to throw away broken umbrellas. Mina suggested a repair event. A local shop owner showed volunteers how to replace small parts. At the first event, they repaired eighteen umbrellas but could not fix four. Those four were sent to a recycling center. The next event will be in November. Students should book a place by email because only twelve volunteers can work safely in the room.

passages.q: 最初の行事で修理できた傘の数を数字で答えなさい。
passages.why: repaired eighteen umbrellasが根拠です。fourは修理できなかった数です。

passages.why: book a place by emailが根拠。作業スペースの安全を保つため予約します。

passages: Leo did not enjoy reading long books. His teacher suggested a short nature guide. Leo took it to a riverside park and looked for birds shown in the pictures. He became interested in learning more and borrowed a longer book about birds. He now visits the park twice a month. On rainy days, he reads at home instead. He says the first guide helped him connect reading with something he could actually see.

passages.q: 最初にLeoへ提案した人を英語1語で答えなさい。
passages.why: His teacher suggested a short nature guideが根拠です。

passages.q: 毎月、公園へ行く回数を数字で答えなさい。

writing.q: 友達へのメールです。英語30語程度で返事を書き、二つの質問両方に答えなさい。Hi! I want to learn a new sport. What sport do you recommend? Why do you recommend it?
writing.answer: I recommend badminton. You can play it indoors, so rain is not a problem. It is also easy to start with friends. I think you will enjoy playing it.
writing.why: 模範例は一例です。競技名と薦める理由の両方が必要。理由が競技の特徴とつながっているか、主語と動詞があるかを確認します。
accepted: I recommend badminton. You can play it indoors, so rain is not a problem. It is also easy to start with friends. I think you will enjoy playing it.

writing.q: Do you think students should help clean their local parks? 英語40語程度で自分の考えと理由二つを書きなさい。
writing.answer: Yes, I do. First, clean parks are safer for children because there is less trash on the ground. Second, students can learn to take care of their town. Working together can also help them make new friends.
writing.why: YesでもNoでもよい。立場、異なる理由二つ、理由とのつながりを評価します。模範例と同じ文章である必要はありません。
accepted: Yes, I do. First, clean parks are safer for children because there is less trash on the ground. Second, students can learn to take care of their town. Working together can also help them make new friends.

questions.q: 最初にLeoへ提案した人を英語1語で答えなさい。
questions.why: His teacher suggested a short nature guideが根拠です。

questions.q: 毎月、公園へ行く回数を数字で答えなさい。
questions.why: twice a monthは月に2回です。雨の日は家で読書します。

questions.q: 友達へのメールです。英語30語程度で返事を書き、二つの質問両方に答えなさい。Hi! I want to learn a new sport. What sport do you recommend? Why do you recommend it?
questions.answer: I recommend badminton. You can play it indoors, so rain is not a problem. It is also easy to start with friends. I think you will enjoy playing it.
questions.why: 模範例は一例です。競技名と薦める理由の両方が必要。理由が競技の特徴とつながっているか、主語と動詞があるかを確認します。
accepted: I recommend badminton. You can play it indoors, so rain is not a problem. It is also easy to start with friends. I think you will enjoy playing it.

questions.q: Do you think students should help clean their local parks? 英語40語程度で自分の考えと理由二つを書きなさい。
questions.answer: Yes, I do. First, clean parks are safer for children because there is less trash on the ground. Second, students can learn to take care of their town. Working together can also help them make new friends.
questions.why: YesでもNoでもよい。立場、異なる理由二つ、理由とのつながりを評価します。模範例と同じ文章である必要はありません。
accepted: Yes, I do. First, clean parks are safer for children because there is less trash on the ground. Second, students can learn to take care of their town. Working together can also help them make new friends.

pre2.label: 準2級

cloze.q: The museum offers free ( admission / attention / direction ) to children under six.
cloze.why: 入場を表すadmission。attentionは注意、directionは方向です。

cloze.q: The heavy snow caused a ( delay / habit / purpose ) in train services.
cloze.why: 列車の運行が遅れることはdelay。habitは習慣、purposeは目的です。

cloze.q: We need to ( reduce / refuse / replace ) food waste by buying only what we need.
cloze.why: 必要な分だけ買うことで食品廃棄を減らすのでreduceです。

cloze.q: Our prediction was wrong: the results were different from what we had ( expected / protected / collected ).
cloze.why: 予想していた内容との違いなのでexpected。protectは守る、collectは集めるです。

cloze.q: The match was put ( off / out / away ) until Monday because of the storm.
cloze.why: put offは延期する。put outは火を消す、put awayは片付けるです。

cloze.q: Although the route was longer, it was much ( safe / safely / safer ).
cloze.why: wasの補語は形容詞。muchは比較級saferを強めます。

cloze.q: I wish I ( have / had / will have ) more time to practice now.
cloze.why: 現在の事実と異なる願いはI wishと過去形で表します。

cloze.q: By the time I arrived, the meeting had already ( begun / began / begin ).
cloze.why: hadと過去分詞で到着前の開始を表します。beginの過去分詞はbegunです。

cloze.q: She is used to ( work / working / worked ) with people from different countries.
cloze.why: be used toは「慣れている」。このtoは前置詞なのでing形を続けます。

cloze.q: The device allows users ( check / checking / to check ) the temperature remotely.
cloze.why: allow人to動詞で、人が何かできるようにすることを表します。

order.q: 「彼はその申し出を受け入れるかどうか決めていません。」( the offer / decided / he / whether to accept / hasn't )
order.answer: He hasn't decided whether to accept the offer.
order.why: whether to acceptは受け入れるかどうか。hasn't decidedの目的語になります。
accepted: He hasn't decided whether to accept the offer.

order.q: 「悪天候にもかかわらず、彼らは調査を続けました。」( the survey / despite / continued / they / the bad weather )
order.answer: Despite the bad weather, they continued the survey.
order.why: despiteのあとに名詞句を置き、逆接を表します。文末に置いても認めます。
accepted: Despite the bad weather, they continued the survey.
They continued the survey despite the bad weather.

order.q: 「その説明は、私が理解できるほど明確でした。」( for me / clear enough / the explanation / to understand / was )
order.answer: The explanation was clear enough for me to understand.
order.why: 形容詞enough for人to動詞で、人がその動作をできる程度であることを表します。
accepted: The explanation was clear enough for me to understand.

order.q: 「誰がその展示を担当するのか教えてください。」( the display / tell me / in charge of / please / who is )
order.answer: Please tell me who is in charge of the display.
order.why: 間接疑問はwho isの語順。be in charge ofは担当しているという意味です。
accepted: Please tell me who is in charge of the display.

passages: Westfield residents opened a shared freezer for extra garden vegetables. At first, anyone could leave food without a label. Volunteers soon found that this made it difficult to check how long food had been stored. They introduced labels showing the date and the name of the vegetable. Cooked meals are not accepted because the volunteers cannot check all ingredients. The freezer is open three afternoons a week. A nearby cafe pays the electricity bill, while residents take turns cleaning the area.

passages.q: ラベルのない食品では何の確認が難しかったですか。日本語で答えなさい。
passages.answer: 食品がどれくらいの期間保存されていたか
passages.why: how long food had been storedが根拠。種類や量だけを答えると目的を捉えられていません。
accepted: 食品がどれくらいの期間保存されていたか
食品がいつから保存されているか

passages.q: 電気代を払っている施設を英語1語で答えなさい。
passages.why: A nearby cafe pays the electricity billが根拠です。住民は清掃を分担します。

passages: A town tested a late bus for students attending evening classes. The first survey asked whether people wanted the service, and most said yes. However, only a few used it during the first month. A second survey revealed that the bus left ten minutes before many classes ended. The town changed the departure time rather than canceling the route. Passenger numbers then increased. Officials decided to continue the test for three more months before making a final decision.

passages.q: 利用者が少なかった理由を日本語で答えなさい。
passages.answer: 多くの授業が終わる10分前にバスが出発していたから
passages.why: wanted the serviceへの肯定と実際の利用は別。2回目の調査で出発時刻の問題が分かりました。
accepted: 多くの授業が終わる10分前にバスが出発していたから
多くの授業の終了より10分早くバスが出発したから

passages.q: 最終判断の前に、さらに何か月試験運行しますか。数字で答えなさい。
passages.why: for three more monthsが根拠です。first monthは最初の実施期間です。

writing.q: 英語50語程度でメールへの返信を書きなさい。相手の提案に賛成か反対かと理由を述べ、必要な情報を一つ質問しなさい。Our club may hold a weekend event where students exchange books. Do you think this is a good idea?
writing.answer: I think a book exchange is a good idea because students can discover new stories without spending much money. It also gives us a chance to talk about our favorite writers. Could you tell me where we would hold the event? We will need enough space for the books.
writing.why: 賛否、関連する理由、情報を求める質問が必要です。書き手の意図が伝わるかを確認し、例と違う考えでも認めます。
accepted: I think a book exchange is a good idea because students can discover new stories without spending much money. It also gives us a chance to talk about our favorite writers. Could you tell me where we would hold the event? We will need enough space for the books.

writing.q: Should towns provide more places where young people can study after school? 英語60語程度で意見と理由二つを書きなさい。
writing.answer: I think towns should provide more study spaces. First, some students do not have a quiet place at home, so a public space would help them concentrate. Second, students could support each other when they have difficult homework. These spaces should have clear rules so that everyone can use them safely and comfortably. This would make them more useful.
writing.why: YesでもNoでもよい。理由二つが別の観点か、意見を支えているか、文同士がつながるかを評価します。模範例は唯一の正答ではありません。
accepted: I think towns should provide more study spaces. First, some students do not have a quiet place at home, so a public space would help them concentrate. Second, students could support each other when they have difficult homework. These spaces should have clear rules so that everyone can use them safely and comfortably. This would make them more useful.
